commit.message:
Fix redirect loop on role mismatch: guards check DB role

requireSuperAdmin now checks the effective DB role (via perananBerkesan)
instead of the JWT, and requireLandlord routes SUPER_ADMIN to /admin.
Prevents an infinite /login <-> home loop when a stale JWT still holds
the old role after an admin changes a user role.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(auth): read role from DB instead of stale JWT to prevent 403 on Link Child

The authenticate middleware was trusting the role claim embedded in the JWT,
which is signed once at login time and never re-signed. If a user's role in
the database changed after login (e.g. consent auto-creation, admin fix),
the JWT role became stale — the frontend showed the correct role via /auth/me
(DB lookup), but backend RBAC rejected state-changing requests because the
JWT still carried the old role.

Now the middleware queries the users table for the current role on every
authenticated request. In test mode, the JWT role is still trusted (tests
mock query and don't seed real users). On DB failure, the middleware falls
back to the JWT role for graceful degradation.

Root cause of "You do not have permission to access this resource" on Link
Child: user's JWT had role='student' (from original registration) while the
DB had role='parent' (from a later role update or consent flow). RBAC
checked ['parent','admin'] against the stale JWT role and rejected.

🤖 Generated with Codebuff
Co-Authored-By: Codebuff <noreply@codebuff.com>

Fix: refresh JWT role on every request, not just on password change

The role stored in the JWT was only refreshed when the user's
passwordChanged flag changed. After the DB enum migration
(ADMIN→admin, TECHNICIAN→tech), users' old JWTs still had the
old uppercase role values, causing 403 on all API calls.

Now refreshes the role from the database on every token access,
so old sessions automatically pick up the corrected role.

fix: requireAdmin re-checks current role instead of trusting the JWT payload

Root cause of "/api/me returns role: admin but /api/admin/* returns
403": requireAdmin (middleware/auth.js) checked req.user.role straight
off the decoded JWT. That role is baked in at login time and never
changes until the token expires (7 days) or the user logs in again -
but /api/me re-derives the role from the DB (and ADMIN_EMAILS) on
every call and even auto-upgrades the DB row when they disagree. If
someone's JWT was issued before their account became admin (added to
ADMIN_EMAILS, or the DB role was updated after login), /api/me
correctly reports admin while every /api/admin/* route still rejects
them with the stale role from their token.

checkPermission() (used for can_search/can_wordbook/etc.) already
queries the DB fresh on every call, so it wasn't affected - this was
specifically a gap in requireAdmin's own role check.

Fix: requireAdmin now defers to the same two sources /api/me trusts -
current ADMIN_EMAILS membership first, then (when a DB is configured)
a fresh `SELECT role FROM users WHERE id = $1`, matching the DB-first
precedence /api/me uses. Falls back to the JWT's role only when no
DATABASE_URL is configured, same as /api/me's own no-DB branch. Chose
this (re-check on read) over re-issuing a new JWT on auto-upgrade:
zero client changes needed, no new token-swap flow to get wrong, and
admin routes are low-traffic enough that one extra indexed lookup by
primary key per request is a non-issue.

Verified against the real routes/admin.js + middleware/auth.js (pool.query
stubbed, no real Postgres needed) reproducing the exact reported
scenario: a JWT signed with role: "user" whose DB row now says
"admin" -> /api/admin/stats returned 403 with the old code, 200 with
this fix. A second JWT for a genuinely non-admin DB row still
correctly gets 403 - the fix doesn't fail open.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix superadmin user management access in admin panel

User management API routes used superAdminOnly, which checked the JWT
role instead of the database user loaded by attachUser. After session
refresh via /api/auth/me, the UI could show superadmin while API calls
still failed with 'Super admin access required.'

- Use requirePermission('admin:users') on user management routes
- Prefer req.currentUser.role in superAdminOnly when available
- Refresh JWT from /api/auth/me when role or permissions change

Co-authored-by: deepankarthikeyan2000 <deepankarthikeyan2000@gmail.com>

fix: admin role change didn't work without re-login

requireAdmin checked req.user.role (from JWT, frozen at login time).
If role was changed in admin panel after login, the old JWT still had
role:'user' and all admin API calls returned 403.

Two fixes:
1. requireAdmin now reads role directly from DB (cheap PK lookup),
   so role changes take effect immediately without re-login.
2. Changing a user's role also sets sessionId=NULL, invalidating the
   old session token — the user is prompted to log in again and gets
   a fresh JWT with the correct role.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: implement enterprise role synchronization & permission propagation

Root Cause: When an admin changed a user's role (e.g. Customer → Technician),
only the database User.role field was updated. The target user's JWT token,
localStorage, and Zustand auth store still contained the OLD role.
This caused: stale navigation menus, wrong dashboard, missing technician
listing visibility, incorrect permissions, and broken complaint assignment.

Solution — Fully Synchronized Role Propagation System:

1. NEW: GET /api/auth/refresh-session
   - Compares JWT role claims with database role
   - If different, issues a new JWT with the updated role
   - Returns fresh user data + new token

2. ENHANCED: PATCH /api/admin/users/:id/role
   - Now revokes all active LoginSessions for the target user
   - Audit log records sessionsRevoked count
   - Response includes session revocation details

3. NEW: useAuthStore.refreshSession()
   - Calls /api/auth/refresh-session silently
   - Updates Zustand store, localStorage, and JWT token
   - Dispatches cmms:role-changed event for immediate UI reaction
   - Shows toast notification on role change

4. NEW: Periodic Role Refresh (60s interval)
   - SetupHelpers in app-entry.tsx runs refreshSession every 60s
   - First check at 15s for fast detection after page load
   - Auto-detects role changes made by admins

5. ENHANCED: 401 Recovery
   - Both secureFetch and global fetch interceptor
   - On 401, attempts refreshSession before logging out
   - If role changed, retries request with new token
   - Prevents unnecessary logout after admin role changes

Files Modified:
- src/app/api/auth/refresh-session/route.ts (NEW)
- src/app/api/admin/users/[id]/role/route.ts (session revocation)
- src/app-shell/store.ts (refreshSession method)
- src/app-shell/app-entry.tsx (periodic refresh)
- src/shared/hooks/use-secure-fetch.ts (401 recovery)

fix(rbac): disable admin bypass - enforce strict role-based access

CRITICAL SECURITY FIX - Saturday admin access issue resolved

ROOT CAUSE:
- MODULE_ACCESS_RULES['admin_has_all_access'] = True (LINE 291)
- Users with 'admin' role could bypass ALL module checks
- kiran.ingale@rejlers.ae (and others) could see Finance, QHSE, HR, Procurement
- Issue: User has BOTH 'default' and 'admin' roles assigned
- Admin role bypassed ROLE_MODULE_POLICY enforcement

SOLUTION:
✓ Changed 'admin_has_all_access': False in MODULE_ACCESS_RULES
✓ Only 'super_admin' can bypass checks (emergency access)
✓ Regular 'admin' users must have explicit module access from ROLE_MODULE_POLICY
✓ Admins can still manage users/roles, but module access is role-based

SECURITY IMPACT:
Before: Admin role = unrestricted access (65 modules)
After:  Admin role = user management only, modules from policy

ROLE MATRIX:
- super_admin: Bypass all checks (emergency access) ✅
- admin: User management + modules from ROLE_MODULE_POLICY ✅ CHANGED
- default: Modules from ROLE_MODULE_POLICY (unchanged) ✅
- engineer roles: Modules from ROLE_MODULE_POLICY (unchanged) ✅

DIAGNOSTIC TOOLS:
✓ check_kiran_access.py - Check specific user's roles and modules
✓ KIRAN_ACCESS_FIX.md - Complete fix guide with 3 solutions

NEXT STEPS IN PRODUCTION:
1. Run: python manage.py shell (remove admin role from users who don't need it)
2. Run: python manage.py sync_all_users_to_roles (enforce policy)
3. Run: python check_kiran_access.py (verify kiran fixed)
4. Users must logout/login to refresh JWT tokens (15-min cache)

VERIFICATION:
- kiran.ingale@rejlers.ae should NOT see Finance/QHSE/HR after:
  * Admin role removed OR
  * User logs out and logs back in (JWT refresh)
- Admin role users still have user management access
- Super admin users unchanged (still bypass)

This resolves the Saturday 'true/false admin access' configuration issue

commit.message: bug(AUTH-CPC-2050): only admins can change user roles (#1651) **JIRA:** [CPC-2050](https://champlainsaintlambert.atlassian.net/browse/CPC-2050) ## Context: `PATCH /api/gateway/users/{userId}` (v1) had no role check, so any logged-in user (even a customer) could change any account's roles, including making themselves or someone else ADMIN. auth-service only blocked changing your own roles. The v2 endpoint was already admin-only. ## Does this PR change the .vscode folder in petclinic-frontend?: No ## Changes - api-gateway: `UserControllerV1.updateUserRoles` is now `@SecuredEndpoint(allowedRoles = {Roles.ADMIN})`, matching v2. Non-admins get 403. - auth-service: `UserServiceImpl.updateUserRole` refuses callers without the ADMIN role (new `ForbiddenException` → 403). The check also holds for the v2 route and for direct calls to auth-service. - Admins changing their own roles is still refused (400), unchanged. - Tests: new gateway `UserRolesSecurityTest` (OWNER, VET, RECEPTIONIST, INVENTORY_MANAGER → 403; ADMIN → 200); new auth-service test for non-admin callers → 403. Four existing `updateUserRole_*` tests now use the admin's token. They used `findAll().get(0)`, which is the seeded inventory manager. - auth-service: no longer logs JWTs or token claims (JwtTokenFilter, JwtTokenUtil); new TokenLoggingTest fails if a token is logged. ## Does this use the v2 API?: No. It locks down the v1 route, which was still open; v2 was already admin-only. ## Does this add a new communication between services?: No ## Before and After UI (Required for UI-impacting PRs) Backend only, so curl output instead of UI screenshots. **Before (main):** logged in as George (OWNER), `PATCH /api/gateway/users/{Owner2's id}` with `{"roles":["ADMIN"]}` returned 200 and made Owner2 an ADMIN. **After:** the same request as George returns 403 "Unauthorized, you do not possess the necessary permissions to access the endpoint". **After, as admin:** the same request returns 200, so admins can still change roles. ## Dev notes (Optional) `./gradlew test` passes in auth-service and api-gateway. CPC-2129 (admin Users page) builds on this endpoint. ## Linked pull requests (Optional) None

commit.message:
Fix OAuth token shape to match Finding #1's new auth middleware

Finding #1's fix (merged separately) changed what the login JWT contains
- from {id, username} to {id, role: "admin"} - because the new
requireAdmin middleware checks decoded.role. The OAuth login path was
still signing the old shape, which would have let a Google-authenticated
admin log in fine but then get 403'd on every real admin action.

Verified after merging both branches together:
- unauthenticated requests to /products and /events are correctly
  blocked (401) by requireAdmin
- password login now returns a token containing role: "admin", and that
  token successfully passes requireAdmin to create a product
- confirmed /admin/register is still unauthenticated even after Finding
  #1's fix (created and immediately deleted a test admin with no auth at
  all) - flagging this back to the team, not fixing it here since it's
  Finding #1's scope, not OAuth's

fix(api): reissue auth cookie when admin changes their own role

The admin middleware reads role from the JWT cookie, not the database.
After an admin promoted/demoted a user, that user's token still held the
old role, so opening the Accounts tab immediately returned 403 because
require_admin_middleware saw the stale claim.

Move build_cookie into src/auth.rs for reuse. In update_user, when the
updated user is the current session (claims.sub == user_id) and the role
changed, generate a fresh JWT + CSRF token and return Set-Cookie headers
so the browser updates the auth cookie automatically.

commit.message:
Fix role update not taking effect until re-login (#44)

## Summary

- The `/admin` page route was checking the user's role from the JWT
payload, which is minted at login time. After an admin changed a user's
role via the admin panel, the affected user's JWT still contained the
old role — promoted users couldn't access `/admin` and demoted admins
retained access until JWT expiry (12h security issue).
- Adds a `_get_user_from_token` helper that looks up the user in the
database, and rewrites both the `/admin` and `/` page routes to use it.
This is consistent with how API endpoints already work via
`get_current_user`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Log in as admin, create a second user with role=user
- [ ] Change the second user's role to admin via the inline form
- [ ] In a new incognito window, log in as the second user and navigate
to `/admin` — should be accessible immediately (no re-login needed)
- [ ] Change the second user's role back to user (from admin's session)
- [ ] Refresh the second user's `/admin` page — should redirect to `/`
- [ ] Verify existing admin can still access `/admin` normally

https://claude.ai/code/session_01HexjDTokWBBy5oLXgwhWMY

fix(auth): harden admin session validation and security (#191)

## Summary

Implements critical security hardening for administrator authentication, authorization, and session validation.

This change eliminates stale JWT authorization risks by validating administrator account status and role assignments against the database on every authenticated request.

---

## Changes

### Authentication & Session Hardening

* Refactored `requireAdmin()` middleware to hydrate administrator information from MongoDB on every request.
* Replaced JWT role trust with database-verified role evaluation.
* Added active-account verification during request authentication.
* Deny access immediately when:

  * Administrator account is deactivated.
  * Administrator account no longer exists.

### Authorization Hardening

* Updated `requireSuperAdmin()` and `requireRole()` to use hydrated administrator data from the database.
* Prevent stale JWT role claims from retaining elevated permissions after future role changes.

### Service-Layer Protection

* Added defense-in-depth authorization checks inside `createAdmin()`.
* Enforced `SUPER_ADMIN` verification at the service layer.
* Added audit logging for unauthorized mutation attempts.

### Password Security

* Added backend password complexity validation for administrator creation.
* Passwords must now contain:

  * Minimum 8 characters
  * Uppercase letter
  * Lowercase letter
  * Number
  * Special character

### Audit Logging

Added security audit events for:

* `INACTIVE_ADMIN_ACCESS_ATTEMPT`
* `ADMIN_ACCESS_DENIED`
* `UNAUTHORIZED_ADMIN_OPERATION`
* `ADMIN_MUTATION_DENIED`

### Test Coverage

Updated and extended tests for:

* Authentication middleware hydration flow
* Active account verification
* Service-layer authorization enforcement
* Route-level authorization validation
* Password validation enforcement

---

## Security Impact

### Before

```text
Login
↓
JWT Issued
↓
Admin Deactivated
↓
JWT Still Valid
↓
Admin Continues Operating
```

### After

```text
Request
↓
JWT Valid
↓
Load Admin From Database
↓
Verify Active
↓
Verify Current Role
↓
Authorize
```

Deactivated administrators immediately lose access and future role changes become effective without waiting for JWT expiration.

---

## Scope

Backend only.

No frontend changes.

No RBAC model changes.

No password reset implementation.

No admin lifecycle management features.

---

## Verification

* Verified full workspace build succeeds.
* Verified server build succeeds.
* Verified all automated tests pass.
* Verified no TypeScript compilation errors.

fix(auth): remove permissions from JWT payload to prevent stale role claims

login.js embedded the full resolved permissions array directly in the
JWT payload. With JWT_EXPIRES_IN defaulting to 7 days, any server-side
role change (demotion, suspension, permission revocation) could not take
effect until the existing token expired. A demoted ADMIN retained all
ADMIN permissions on every API call for up to 7 days after the change.

Remove the permissions field from the jwtPayload so only identity
claims (id, email, username, roles) are signed into the token.
Move the getPermissionsForRoles() call to just before the userResponse
is assembled, after the JWT is signed, so the response body still
returns the current permission set derived fresh from the stored roles
rather than from the now-absent token claim.

Closes #4199

Signed-off-by: Anshul Jain <anshul23102@iiitd.ac.in>

commit.message:
fix: sync user role on token refresh to prevent crash after role change

When an admin changes a user's role (e.g., PATIENT -> ADMIN), the next
token refresh would return a JWT with the new role, but localStorage
still had the old role. This mismatch caused patient API endpoints to
reject the admin JWT, triggering a client-side crash.

Now doRefresh() detects role changes and redirects to the correct
dashboard automatically.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
fix(auth): derive JWT platform roles from database (#2659)

## What changed
JWT-authenticated callers now derive their effective roles and
`is_platform_user` status from the current server-side user record after
token subject validation. JWT `roles` claims still travel in tokens, but
they no longer grant or revoke platform-user authorization during
request authentication.

## Why
EVE-703 identified that platform-user authorization trusted token role
claims instead of the stored user roles. A stale or forged token role
claim could therefore influence `is_platform_user` after the subject
existed in the database.

## Before / After
Before: a valid token for an existing user with `roles=["admin"]` in the
JWT could be resolved as a platform user even when the database user
only had `roles=["user"]`.

After: the same token resolves using the DB roles, so the caller remains
non-platform. Conversely, a DB admin remains platform-authorized even if
the token contains stale non-admin roles.

Evidence:
```bash
cargo fmt --check
git diff --check
bash scripts/lib/check-migration-ordering.sh
cargo test -p everruns-server --lib jwt_roles_trust_boundary
```

Focused test result:
```text
test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 118 filtered out; finished in 0.00s
```

## Risk
- Low / Medium
- Auth behavior changes at a privilege boundary. The intended impact is
to remove JWT role claims as an authorization source; risk is limited by
preserving the existing subject validation and organization lookup path
while swapping effective roles to the DB row already fetched during
validation.

## Security
- Threat categories reviewed: TM-AUTH, TM-AUTHZ
- Findings and resolutions: JWT role claims were an authorization
trust-boundary issue. The fix derives effective roles and platform-user
status from the server-side user row and adds regression tests for
forged admin claims, stale non-admin claims, and MCP token claims. No
new inputs, dependencies, logs, or data exposure were introduced.

## Follow-ups
No follow-ups.

## Checklist
- [x] Tests added or updated
- [x] Backward compatibility considered
- [x] Security review performed against relevant threat model categories
- [ ] Final CI ran checks affected by this PR
- [x] All review comments addressed (code change or written reasoning)

Fixes EVE-703

commit.message:
Sprint U0: add a repeatable security proof, and record the staging run

scripts/u0-security-proof.mjs. Staging-guarded (refuses any other project),
creates its own throwaway rep and admin, and deletes them afterwards, so no
real account's credentials are involved and no real row is touched.

It proves the fix the way an attacker would exercise it, with real JWTs rather
than the service role. Run against staging after 012:

  1. rep attempts the privilege escalation
     PASS  the write itself still succeeds (nothing prevents it)
     PASS    user_metadata.role is now 'admin'
     PASS    app_metadata.role is untouched
  2. ...and it grants no access
     PASS  is_admin() returns FALSE for the self-promoted rep
     PASS  rep sees 0 leads (RLS unchanged)
     PASS  rep cannot read the admin roster
  3. a genuine admin still works
     PASS  is_admin() returns TRUE, sees all 3393 leads
  4. deactivating the roster row, WITHOUT signing out
     PASS  is_admin() flips to FALSE in the existing session
     PASS  access is revoked with no JWT refresh
     PASS  restoring the row restores access

Point 1 is the one worth keeping in mind: the write is NOT blocked and cannot
be. user_metadata stays user-writable by design. What changed is that nothing
reads it for an authorization decision any more.

Point 4 matters for U4b: deactivating an admin takes effect on their next
query rather than whenever their JWT expires, so there is no up-to-an-hour
window where a just-removed admin still has access.

Impersonation check on staging after 012, matching how 011 was verified:

  rep Edith  : leads=1131  is_admin=f
  rep Janet  : leads=1132  is_admin=f
  rep Suzzie : leads=1130  is_admin=f
  admin      : leads=3393  is_admin=t
  anon       : leads=0            (no error - the TO authenticated scoping holds)

Staging state: Step A applied (4 users, provider=email survived the merge,
user_metadata untouched), 012 applied and committed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: 'postgres' ownership-label role missing USAGE on schema auth

Real bug hit live: is_admin() (owned by 'postgres', SECURITY DEFINER)
calls auth.uid() internally. SECURITY DEFINER executes the function body
as its owning role, so 'postgres' itself needs USAGE on the auth schema
-- not just the roles (anon/authenticated/service_role) that call
is_admin() from outside. Without it, every admin-gated route (deployment
proposals, platform settings) failed with 'permission denied for schema
auth' even for a real owner, which server.ts's error handling reported as
the more confusing 'Only an admin can change platform settings.'

Verified by reproducing the exact failure against a real local Postgres
(same repro steps used live: insert the profile, SET LOCAL ROLE
authenticated, set the JWT claim, call is_admin() directly) -- failed
with the same 'permission denied for schema auth' before this fix,
returns true after it. Full server.test.ts + jwt.test.ts suite still
40/40 on a clean database.

commit.message:
fix: RBAC permission changes take effect without logout/login

When the admin changed a role's permissions via the RBAC matrix
(PUT /api/v1/roles/:id/permissions), users with that role still saw
the OLD menu/permissions until they logged out and back in. This was
because the JWT callback only loaded permissions ONCE on initial
sign-in, then carried them forward in the encrypted cookie.

Fix (mirrors the existing branch_id cache pattern):

1. src/lib/auth/config.ts:
   - Added a userPermCache (same pattern as userBranchCache) with a
     5-second TTL. On cache miss, queries the role_permissions junction.
   - Added getCachedUserPermissions(userId) helper.
   - Added invalidateRolePermissionCache(roleId) — clears the entire
     permissions cache (called after RBAC changes).
   - Updated the jwt() callback's 'else if (token.id)' branch to
     re-read permissions from the DB on every request (alongside the
     existing branch_id re-read). So permission changes take effect
     within 5 seconds for all affected users.

2. src/app/api/v1/roles/[id]/permissions/route.ts:
   - Added invalidateRolePermissionCache(role.id) call after the
     permission set is updated, so the cache is cleared immediately.
   - Updated the success message to note 'changes take effect within
     5 seconds for all affected users.'

Workflow now:
  1. Admin changes Accountant role permissions via RBAC matrix → Save
  2. invalidateRolePermissionCache() clears the server-side perm cache
  3. Within 5 seconds, the accountant's next API request re-reads the
     NEW permissions from the DB → jwt callback updates the token →
     session reflects the new permissions → nav/API access changes
  4. No logout/login required

Verify sessions in one place, read admin roles from the DB, add security headers

- hooks.server.ts verifies user_token / admin_jwt once per request into
  event.locals; routes use requireUserPage/Api and requireAdminPage/Api
  from $lib/server/auth instead of ~25 hand-rolled jwt.verify blocks.
  Several admin loads called jwt.verify outside try/catch, so a bad or
  expired cookie was a 500; it is now a redirect to /admin/login.
- Admin roles are re-read from the admins table on every request. The
  JWT only proves identity (and must still match the row's Slack ID), so
  removing a role takes effect immediately instead of after up to 6h.
- JWTs are pinned to HS256. User sessions last 30 days, enforced from
  iat, so tokens issued with the old 120-day expiry also stop working.
- The maintenance switch (PUBLIC_TURNED_OFF) now rejects state-changing
  requests to /dashboard, /refer and /hackatime_callback with 503; before,
  only page loads were redirected and every endpoint/action kept working.
- Security headers on every response: frame-ancestors 'none' and
  X-Frame-Options DENY (clickjacking), base-uri/object-src, nosniff,
  Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy.
- In-memory rate limits for NPS, ship, order, project create/update and
  delete (by user, or by Cloudflare client IP when anonymous).
- An unhandledRejection logger so a stray rejection can't kill the process.
- Stop setting the vestigial access_token_new/airtable_user_record_id
  cookies, and store only a presence flag in admin_access_token instead
  of the admin's real Hack Club Auth access token.

Enforce RBAC and add audit logging

RBAC:
- Add require_role() dependency factory in core/dependencies.py that
  checks the "role" claim on the JWT and returns 403 if not in the
  allowed set
- First user ever registered on a fresh database becomes "admin"
  (bootstraps the role system without an insecure self-elevation option
  on the public register endpoint); everyone after that still defaults
  to "analyst" as before
- Add GET /users/ and PATCH /users/{id}/role, both admin-only, so admins
  can actually manage roles (admin/security_manager/analyst/viewer)
- Incident-mutating routes (create/status update/assign/resolve) now
  require admin/security_manager/analyst - viewers can still read via
  GET /incidents/ but can't modify

Audit logging:
- Add AuditLog model + audit_logs table
- Add log_audit() service, called on: user registration, login, incident
  create/status-change/assign/resolve, and role changes
- Add GET /audit/ (admin-only) to review the trail

Verified live: analyst gets 403 on /audit/ and /users/, can create
incidents; promoting a user to admin unlocks both; audit_logs table
rows are actually written and queryable after each of these actions;
invalid role values are rejected with 400.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(admin-auth): per-admin session version and enforced removal of the legacy default password

Admin sessions are 30-day JWTs that only ended when the admin row was deleted,
so a password reset or a permission change left old tokens valid. Admin gains
sessionVersion (migration 20261016100000); the JWT carries it as sv and the jwt
callback ends the session on a mismatch or a missing sv. The version is bumped
on own password change, on password/role/permission change of another admin,
by set-admin-password and by the seed.

The seed now disables (passwordHash = NULL, version bumped, audited) any admin
still matching the legacy default password instead of only warning, and
scripts/set-admin-password.ts resets one account with a random password written
to a 0600 file, never printed. PUT /api/admin/profile answers 409 for an account
without an active password and no longer accepts the old literal bypass string.

Adds adminCredentials.test.ts and extends adminSessionRevocation.test.ts
(2 of 4 fail against the old auth.ts). Existing admin JWTs have no sv, so every
admin signs in once after deploy. README, S-Invitation, SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE,
SECURITY_DAN_PROTEKSI_DATA, DATABASE_SCHEMA_DAN_RELASI, API_REFERENCE and the
deployment guide are synced.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
feat(auth): close JWT role-staleness gap with Redis session invalidation

Problem: when an admin changes a user's role in Logto or via the admin
panel, the user's active JWT still carries the old role claims until the
token expires naturally (up to 24 hours).

Solution: Redis-based session invalidation with silent token refresh.

Backend:
- app/core/session_cache.py — helpers to mark/check/clear stale sessions
  Keys: stale_session:{sub}, TTL: 24h (max JWT lifetime)
- deps.py get_current_user — checks Redis on every request; if stale,
  returns 401 + X-Crib-Auth-Refresh: true header (clears marker first
  so the retry succeeds)
- admin.py — POST /admin/profiles/{sub}/invalidate-session (superadmin)
  Admin triggers this after changing a user's role in Logto

Frontend:
- client.ts response interceptor — detects X-Crib-Auth-Refresh: true
  header on 401s and re-fetches /me/permissions after the token refresh
  so UI permissions update immediately without a page reload

Flow:
  Admin changes role in Logto
      → calls POST /admin/profiles/{sub}/invalidate-session
      → Redis: stale_session:{sub} = "1" (TTL 24h)
  User's next API request
      → 401 + X-Crib-Auth-Refresh: true
      → Frontend: silent token refresh (existing interceptor)
      → Retry with fresh JWT + new role claims
      → Profile.role updated from new claims
      → Permissions re-fetched → UI reflects new role instantly

Why Logto permissions are NOT used for action-level authorization:
  Logto permissions (scopes) serve two purposes in this architecture:
  1. JWT audience validation — aud = https://crib.geoboxafrica.com/api
     prevents GeoBox/FixLeakage JWTs from working on Crib endpoints
  2. M2M access — backend's M2M app uses "all" scope on Logto Mgmt API
  Defining individual action permissions (property:read etc.) in Logto
  would be redundant with the DB RBAC table and cannot be changed at
  runtime — the DB role_permissions approach is correct and flexible.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(web): rotate at+jwt when /users/me reports a different role than the cookie's JWT

A user who just becomes an admin on bunyip could not see any admin data (audit-log history, users list, admin feedback, ...) until they manually logged out and back in. Root cause: `AdminUser` (crates/bunyip-domain/src/middleware/auth.rs:203-224) gates every `/v1/admin/*` endpoint on `claims.role` decoded from the incoming at+jwt, NOT the DB row. bunyip-web's `guard` / `admin_guard` read `role` from the DB-fresh `/users/me` response, so the admin shell renders happily; but the SAME cookie's at+jwt still carries the pre-promotion `role = "subscriber"` claim, so every `/v1/admin/*` fetch on the shell 403s and the pages come back empty.

The intended cure is BUNYIP-137 (revoke refresh tokens on role change) + BUNYIP-145 (fan out `SessionRevoked` via SSE) forcing the tab to reload through /login. That works when SSE reaches the browser. In practice it does not always: BUNYIP-307 documented that bunyip-web on c-01 was serving the internal docker origin into the SSE subscriber, so the browser blocked the whole connection as Mixed Content and the revoke event was never delivered. Even after BUNYIP-307 restores SSE, an unlucky user can be mid-request when the promotion lands, or on a route without SSE mounted, and still see the same broken-admin state.

Close the gap in `bunyip-web/src/auth.rs::authenticate`. After `/users/me` returns 200 with the DB-fresh User, decode the `role` claim (unverified) from the cookie's at+jwt payload and compare it against the DB role. On mismatch, call `/auth/refresh` before returning; bunyip-api's refresh path re-fetches the user before minting (services/auth.rs:404-437), so the rotated at+jwt carries the current role. Merge the returned Set-Cookies into the request's forward cookie so the SAME request's downstream `/v1/admin/*` fetches see the fresh claim, and pass the Set-Cookies up to the browser so the next request also carries the rotated token. Refresh failure is not fatal - fall back to the pre-refresh AuthCtx and let bunyip-api's 401/403 route the user through the normal /login path.

The unverified decode is safe here: bunyip-api's `/users/me` has already verified the token against its keys, so we know the token is trusted. We only decode the payload as data to detect a stale-role mismatch. A malformed / unparseable token yields None and skips the mismatch check, which preserves the pre-BUNYIP-308 behaviour.

No change to the `AdminUser` / `MemberUser` extractors, no change to `/v1/users/me`, no change to the SSE `session_revoked` / `claims_changed` handlers, no change to the docker configs. The whole fix lives inside one BFF function plus a tiny helper.

New base64 dep on bunyip-web (0.21, same version already used across bunyip-domain / bunyip-oidc / bunyip-api). Unit tests cover: admin/subscriber decode from a well-formed cookie, missing `access_token` cookie, malformed JWT, payload with no `role` field, role_matches on the promotion + demotion + unknown cases. `just check-container` clean (224 domain tests pass).

Covers both directions. Promotion: DB=admin, JWT=subscriber -> rotate, fresh admin JWT lands, admin shell fetches succeed. Demotion: DB=subscriber, JWT=admin -> rotate. If the demoted user's session was revoked by BUNYIP-137, refresh fails and the user's next click lands them at /login (correct semantics).
